correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the covariance from the Bernoulli number of selected tail elements. Conditional head contrasts give k(s-k)/(s(s-1)) at k=r or r−1, conditional tail contrasts give w/m, and projection onto the block contrast gives (s+m)w(1−w)/(sm). This gives full affine dimension even at s=r. The covariance log determinant has strictly negative second derivative and diverges to −infinity at both endpoints; A+B=(r−1)(s−r+1)>0. At the interior optimum the log determinant derivative is the difference of the two orbit gauges, and their weighted mean is d, so every vertex has gauge d. Averaged containment and trace–determinant AM–GM prove global minimality and force equality only at the stated center and shape; strict convexity excludes other contacts. The stationary polynomial and the cases s=r and s=2r−1 agree. For fixed r, signs of the scaled derivative at fixed interior w give the interior limit or convergence to 1; the rearranged derivative equation gives the supercritical inverse-linear constant. At criticality with m=s/(r−1)+O(1), testing w=1−z/sqrt(s) gives derivative/sqrt(s) tending to rz/(r−1)^2−1/z. Strict monotonicity gives the stated square-root constant.
residual_risks: The critical limit requires the stated finer growth hypothesis; it is not a rate for every sequence with m/s approaching the critical ratio. No formal or expert attestation is claimed.

value.rationale: The canonical matroid family is independently motivated. A unique exact volume/shape and all-contact certificate give usable metric information not fixed by the enclosing sphere or uniform covariance. The change in optimizer scaling shows how head-only vertices can remain contacts although their optimal design mass vanishes, and distinguishes a new quantitative invariant from an already studied threshold ratio.
